rationale: Document describes front/shell companies used to disguise involvement of SDNs/Entity List parties and hide true end users: red flag guidance on shell companies (p.2), the Milandr network's use of two front companies to divert microchips to Russia (p.4), and the Orekhov indictment describing an intermediary that was an empty room in a strip mall (p.5).

citations.quote: Use of corporate vehicles (i.e., legal entities, such as shell companies, and legal arrangements) to obscure (i) ownership, (ii) source of funds, or (iii) countries involved, particularly sanctioned jurisdictions;

Claiming that shell companies located in third countries were intermediaries or end users; in one case, DOJ alleges that only one of the five intermediary parties had any visible signage and consisted of an empty room in a strip mall

rationale: Advisory names historical transshipment points used to redirect controlled items to Russia/Belarus -- China (incl. Hong Kong/Macau), Armenia, Turkey, Uzbekistan (p.3) -- and gives a concrete enforcement case of Vorago Technologies shipping integrated circuit components to Russia via a Bulgarian front company (p.4), matching the routing-through-an-intermediary-jurisdiction mechanism.

citations.quote: Routing purchases through certain transshipment points commonly used to illegally redirect restricted items to Russia or Belarus.  Such locations may include China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and jurisdictions close to Russia, including Armenia, Turkey, and Uzbekistan.

BIS imposed an administrative penalty of $497,000 on Vorago Technologies, an Austin, Texas company, for shipping integrated circuit components, which are critical components in missiles and military satellites, to Russia via a Bulgarian front company.

rationale: Advisory concerns export-control evasion of dual-use/controlled electronics diverted to Russia's defense sector: the Milandr network purchased microchips to divert to Russia (p.4), and the DOJ indictments list dual-use items including advanced semiconductors and microprocessors for missile, radar and satellite systems (p.5). This is the sanctions-family TWIN of TBML007 (Dual Use Goods); SAN007 is preferred because the advisory is a tri-seal Treasury/OFAC, Commerce/BIS and DOJ sanctions and export-control compliance note throughout.

citations.quote: which used a front company to transfer funds from Milandr to another front in a third country, which purchased microchips to divert to Russia.

The sensitive items at issue included advanced electronics and sophisticated testing equipment used in quantum computing, hypersonic, and nuclear weapons development as well as advanced semiconductors and microprocessors used in fighter aircraft, missile systems, smart munitions, radar, and satellites.

rationale: DOJ indictment describes underestimating the purchase price of merchandise on shipping forms by more than five times the actual amount (p.5) -- mispricing the trade transaction itself. This is the sanctions-family TWIN of TBML010 (Sanctions Evasion Through Trade); SAN006 is preferred because the advisory is a tri-seal sanctions/export-control compliance note issued by Treasury, Commerce and DOJ, not a TBML-framed document.

citations.quote: Making false or misleading statements on shipping forms, including underestimating the purchase price of merchandise by more than five times the actual amount

rationale: DOJ indictment tactic list includes using aliases for the identities of intermediaries and end users (p.5) -- engineering names so the true party does not surface to screening or counterparties. The document gives only this single bullet and does not detail a specific fuzzy-match or list-screening defeat mechanism, so confidence is low.

rationale: DOJ indictment describes transferring funds from shell companies in foreign jurisdictions into U.S. bank accounts and quickly forwarding or distributing the funds to obfuscate the audit trail or foreign source of money (p.5) -- a layering chain severing the link between seed funds and destination, in furtherance of a sanctions/export procurement scheme.
